title: Odd Even Jump
summary: Given an integer array arr, determine the number of starting indices from which you can reach the end of the array by making a series of jumps.
statement: Given an integer array arr, determine the number of starting indices from which you can reach the end of the array by making a series of jumps. Jumps are alternated between odd and even types. For odd-numbered jumps, you jump to the smallest index with a value greater than or equal to the current index's value. For even-numbered jumps, you jump to the smallest index with a value less than or equal to the current index's value. If no valid jump is possible from an index, it is not considered a good starting index.
constraints: On an odd jump, choose the smallest later value at least the current value, breaking ties by index.
On an even jump, choose the largest later value at most the current value, again breaking ties by index.
Return how many starting indices eventually reach the final index when jumps alternate odd then even.
hints: Precompute odd and even destinations using value-sorted indices and a monotonic index stack.
Equal values are sorted by increasing index to enforce the nearest-index tie rule.
Work backward: odd-good depends on even-good at its destination, and vice versa.
Every jump destination is deterministic; backward DP therefore marks exactly the starts whose alternating chain reaches the end.
editorial: Every jump destination is deterministic; backward DP therefore marks exactly the starts whose alternating chain reaches the end.

tests.explanation: Only starts at indices one, three, and four reach the end.
Starts zero, one, and four are good.
